analysis.title: Peak Muse? Growth Slows Just As Morgan Stanley Tallies What Meta's "Free" Agent Really Costs
key_insights: Meta launched the Muse agent on September 8. META rose 27% in 12 sessions to a $777.59 peak and the forward multiple went from 14x to 21x.

Hunterbrook (affiliated fund is short META), citing TickerTrends, reported Muse downloads fell 8.1% w/w and daily net user additions slowed 62.4% from the September surge. Downloads were ~169.6K on Oct 6, 21.1% below the 214.9K peak on Sep 24.
Muse DAUs hit a high of 2,730,919 on Oct 6, so the user base is still growing. Net adds averaged ~198K/day Sep 15-22, ~87K/day the next week and ~74K/day in the week to Oct 6.
Estimates of Muse usage disagree: TickerTrends 2.73mn DAUs, Similarweb 2.18mn (Oct 5), Sensor Tower 1.8mn DAUs and 6.6mn downloads. All are under 3mn.

Morgan Stanley (Brian Nowak, Top Pick, $775 target) expects Muse subscription revenue to be small for a while. Monetization via a real-time bidding auction for completed transactions is 'late '27/'28 at the earliest'. BofA also sees no material revenue before 2028.

Morgan Stanley sizes Muse cost-to-serve at $3 to $130 per user per month. CPU sandbox is the larger cost at low usage and GPU inference dominates at full token allowance. The base case (25% of the free allowance) costs $37.12 a month, or $445 a year, which MS calls more of a ceiling.
MS GPU model: GB300 framework, 410,256 GPUs per GW, 3,500 tokens/sec/GPU at 75% utilization, $7.63bn annual infrastructure cost per GW, giving $0.225 per million tokens.

Meta's global ARPU is ~$70 a year per MS. A user at 5% of the allowance ($124/year) costs more to serve than the average ARPU. At 1bn DAUs and the 25% case, cost to serve would be ~$445bn a year versus MS's $256bn 2026 revenue estimate for Meta.
At TickerTrends' 2.73mn DAUs the same $445/year per user is ~$1.2bn annually, small against MS's $209bn of 2027 opex. Slower growth means a smaller compute bill and a smaller future auction.

MS estimates Meta is acquiring enough CPU capacity in 2026 to serve 1bn Muse DAUs at 25% of the weekly token allowance: 20% of AMD's 10.9mn server CPUs, ~360K Nvidia Vera CPUs and 30mn Graviton5 cores, for 643mn vCPUs, or 321mn Muse instances. Demand at 1bn DAUs is ~300mn simultaneous instances, 93% of purchases.

Zerohedge notes MS did not size GPUs for 1bn DAUs. On MS's GPU assumptions, 1bn DAUs at the 25% allowance needs ~38GW of GB300 capacity and 5% usage needs ~7.7GW, versus Meta's Hyperion campus designed for ~5GW. At 2.73mn DAUs the need is ~0.1GW.
MS expects costs are already in its model: $209bn of 2027 opex, $225bn capex in 2026/27 leading to $59bn of 2027 D&A, and $26bn of third-party compute deals in 2027 versus $17bn in 2026.
MS adds a $25tn enterprise TAM to a $30tn consumer TAM. Meta One subscriptions and an API business (100MW of GB300 adds ~4% or ~$1 to 2028 EPS) are cited as monetization paths.
Needham's Laura Martin estimated Apple could lose up to $10bn a year of services revenue (~$7.5bn of EBITDA) if 20% of App Store sales migrated to Muse Connectors.
Amazon blocked Muse on Sep 20. MS reads this as a negotiation and expects the first agentic partnership with AMZN to set precedent. Zerohedge argues slower Muse growth shifts leverage toward Amazon.

MS base case target is $775 (23x average 2027/2028 EPS), bull case $1,000 (28x) and bear case $450 (15x). The stock closed at $718.67 on Friday, 7.6% below its Sep 24 high. Options implied ~36% odds of exceeding $775 within 12 months as of Sep 30.
Street targets: JPMorgan $920, BofA $810, Wells Fargo $796, Tigress $995, Goldman $725. The average is about $800 with virtually no Sells.
META Q3 results on November 4 will test third-party Muse estimates of 1.8mn to 2.7mn DAUs.
Bernstein and BofA's Winnie Wu see Chinese platforms such as Tencent (Xiaowei inside WeChat) as advantaged in agents through closed ecosystems and payment rails.

Goldman's 'Consumer Inertia' short basket GSXUSWCH fell 2.58% on Sep 22. PLNT fell 9.45%, NYT 7.16%, SCHW 6.11%, ALL 5.55% and INTU 3.87%. Zerohedge says a slower Muse ramp buys these names time but does not change direction.

market_movers.rationale: Morgan Stanley's Brian Nowak keeps Meta as a Top Pick, with compute capacity as the moat. Bull case $1,000, bear case $450.
JPMorgan's Doug Anmuth raised the target after Connect and says Meta is not focused on near-term Muse monetization.
BofA reiterated Buy on Sep 22 and says material revenue from ads, subscriptions or commissions is unlikely before 2028.
Goldman's Eric Sheridan reiterated Buy on Sep 13 and cited scale and distribution as hard-to-replicate assets. The stock passed the target eight days later.
Wells Fargo target cited as one of the Street targets above the price.
Tigress target cited as one of the Street targets above the price.
Hunterbrook, whose affiliated fund is short META, reported Muse growth slowing.
Needham's Laura Martin estimated up to $10bn a year of services revenue at risk if 20% of App Store sales move to Muse Connectors.
Fell 9.45% on Sep 22 in Goldman's Consumer Inertia basket on fears that agents cancel memberships.
Fell 7.16% on Sep 22 in Goldman's Consumer Inertia basket.

sector_views.rationale: Goldman's desk was shorting 'Consumer Inertia' names after Muse. Zerohedge says a slower Muse ramp buys time but does not change direction.
Expedia and Booking fell ~4% on fears that agents shop around while OTAs collect rent.
Bernstein says closed ecosystems spanning messaging, payments and e-commerce favor Chinese platforms in agents.

earnings_insights: Meta Q3 results are due November 4, when Meta will be asked for its own Muse numbers.
MS forecasts 2026 Meta revenue of $256bn (estimate), $209bn of 2027 opex (estimate) and $59bn of 2027 D&A (estimate).
MS values META at 23x average 2027/2028 EPS for its $775 base case (estimate). The stock trades at about 21x NTM consensus EPS, versus a ten-year average of 20.0x.
MS estimates 50mn Meta One subscribers add 9.1% (~$3.17) to 2028 EPS and the high end adds 18.1% (~$6.34). An API business adds ~4% (~$1) to 2028 EPS (estimates).

trade_ideas.description: Short 'Consumer Inertia' basket (Goldman GSXUSWCH), including PLNT, NYT, SCHW, ALL, INTU
trade_ideas.rationale: Agentic AI such as Muse can cancel subscriptions and compare quotes, eroding switching-cost premiums.
trade_ideas.risk: A slower Muse ramp buys these companies time.

risk_factors: Muse user growth is slowing (net adds ~74K/day versus ~198K/day at the peak) and usage estimates conflict across vendors.
Muse monetization is not expected before late 2027/2028.
Privacy and security risk, including a zero-day that could hijack Muse accounts, is flagged by Goldman as the biggest risk.
Third parties (Amazon, Costco, Netflix, telecom carriers) restrict agent access.
Per-user compute cost of $3 to $130 a month could exceed ARPU if usage scales.
GPU capacity at 1bn DAUs (~38GW at the 25% case) is not addressed by MS.
The Hunterbrook data comes from a short seller and alternative-data estimates differ by about 50%.
charts_described: MS Exhibit 10 bridges Meta's 2026 CPU purchases to 643mn vCPUs, or 321mn Muse instances, vs 300mn simultaneous instances needed at 1bn DAUs.
MS sensitivity table shows Muse cost to serve from $3 to $130 per user per month, with $37.12 at 25% of the token allowance.
vol_and_positioning: META options implied ~36% odds of exceeding $775 within 12 months and ~14% odds of exceeding $1,000, as of Sep 30 per MS.
Hunterbrook's affiliated fund disclosed a short META position. Zerohedge calls it the first prominent bet against the Muse story.
Goldman's GSXUSWCH 'Consumer Inertia' basket was one of the desk's most actively traded baskets in recent sessions.
META's forward multiple re-rated from 14x to 21x after the August 26 state AG settlement (worth up to ~$17bn).
geopolitical: Amazon blocked Muse from its site on Sep 20, and Costco and Netflix restrictions were reported.
Chinese platforms (Tencent, others) face export controls on compute, per BofA's Winnie Wu.
Chinese mobile internet is dominated by guarded ecosystems such as WeChat and Alipay, which limits outside agents.
cross_bank_references: Zerohedge: 'Morgan Stanley isn't alone on timing. BofA ... said material revenue from ads, subscriptions or commissions is unlikely before 2028.'
Deutsche Bank's Benjamin Black sees Muse reaching up to 8% of Meta's revenue by 2030.
JPMorgan declared Muse 'has the potential to become the most widely used consumer AI application since ChatGPT'.
Goldman's Eric Sheridan called Meta's scale and distribution the 'most difficult-to-replicate assets in the consumer AI agent competition'.

tension_points.bull_case: MS and JPMorgan see Muse as a moat built on compute, with CPUs already bought for 1bn DAUs, a $250bn ad business growing 27% y/y and targets of $775 to $920.
tension_points.bear_case: Hunterbrook/TickerTrends data shows downloads down 21.1% from peak and net adds slowing 62.4%, with usage estimates of only 1.8mn to 2.7mn DAUs against a 14x-to-21x re-rating paid for with a growth story.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Meta's own Muse user numbers at Q3 results on November 4, versus third-party estimates of 1.8mn to 2.7mn DAUs.

tension_points.bull_case: MS expects a real-time bidding auction for completed transactions addressing ~$30tn of consumer spend.
tension_points.bear_case: Revenue is unlikely before late 2027/2028 per MS and BofA, and slower user growth pushes that further out.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Meta reaching a billion-user scale or an agentic partnership with Amazon that sets a precedent structure.

theme_stances.key_argument: Muse download and net-add growth is slowing while MS's capacity analysis assumes 1bn daily users.
MS says the cost of serving Muse is a barrier to entry for smaller players, and Meta has already bought the CPUs for 1bn DAUs.
theme_stances.evidence: cost prohibitive barriers to entry for smaller players to scale a competitive product

theme_stances.key_argument: Agents that can cancel and compare erode the inertia premium in recurring-revenue names.
